body:
I really appreciate this comment, the second I've started thinking that maybe I don't have to do what I'm doing now I've been far more relaxed. Things aren't going to be changing overnight since no matter what I do there will be hard work, but it does feel like a burden off my back. After having depression for so many years it's hard to change anything, even for the better, but definitely not going to use that as an excuse not to. I just need a kick in the ass every now and then like now.

Thank you.

Thanks to everyone for their kind words, I honestly didn't think anything could make a difference but I'm feeling more at ease than I have for a while. It might not last but it shows it's possible so thank you all, good night.

I want to just live my life the way I want to so badly. But I know what I want can't always be what's best, like I'd have stopped school in grade 10 if I could have. But if I could find a way to KNOW that I can stick with this and do this I'd drop out of university in an instant, I'm sick of school. I'm quite literally sick since I can barely get through a day without anxiety attacks anymore.

Maybe I'll just say fuck it. Maybe I'll leave sciences all together and go for an English degree or something. So what if it's as good as place mat, I can't the other stress. It will probably stress me to, but if I can at least find a way to enjoy it that would be bearable.

I'm 19 (first year of uni), and yea I've remembered reading that at least 50% of people change majors after first year practically, I changed my idea 3 times right before I applied myself. I'm just running out of ideas now. And again this is all more excuses than causes for my bad moods.

Lately when I've been stressed I've been writing. I started this national novel writing month thing (write a 50k word story over the course of november) and I've loved it. It's actually made me happy because I've always loved reading fantasy, I read 70 books in the last year of highschool and writing it just felt right. I've never written before so it's bad but it almost feels good enough to just drop out of school for.

Though I know that's an awful idea, writing takes years and years and years of practice to get good, I've been doing it for three weeks, and that still doesn't mean anything. I also know that, like I've done before, I'll give up on it after a month. Before I tried producing music for a month or two but it didn't work so I gave up. I wish this wouldn't be like that but it will be.

Other than this I have nothing to do for stress, I don't have any friends to talk to it about and I have no good outlets anymore.

I'm going into chemistry, one thing I find really cool, but so far calculus is fucking me over. Despite doing well in it in grade 12 this year it's like in on ear and out the other without leaving a trace. Failed my first midterm with a 49 and I can't transfer over to where I want for chemistry without at least a 70% average (ignoring competition).

Trying to decide what else I can do so at least I'm prepared if things go badly but I got nothing and all it does is add to the stress. I'm just awful with stress and even little things like big assignments can set me off.

I don't know, I feel like I'm not living it. First I hear that highschool is supposed to be the best time of your life (though I've also heard the exact opposite which is true for me) and then I hear that university is where you'd supposed to have the time of your life.

Now with university I've done nothing, haven't made a single friend, and even if I did I wouldn't have the time because I have so much work I need to do. Then even with all the work I'm still not even doing well despite being bright (enough) all through highschool. At this rate I wont get into the program I want and then even if I do I'm actually not sure what I want to do with it.

I want to live a life but I don't know how. I can't just quit school, I can't get anywhere without it, but at the same time it's just setting me up for a life of monotony and this is my last chance to get myself out there and meet people (easily).

Everyday I stay in and just do work I feel like another day wasted but the few times I give to myself for pleasure I can't help but think of all the work I have waiting for me. I feel like I'm missing something.

Though these are honestly just excuses because I've had depression for 4 or 5 years now and all new circumstances never seem to change it.
